report.summary: Large change adding the Worker, its Durable Objects, egress, GitHub App and auth. Two blocking problems. (1) The change has no tests and no vitest config. apps/tempo runs `vitest run`, which exits 1 when it finds no test files, so `bun run test` fails. This breaks CLAUDE.md rules 14 and 15 and the 06 definition of done. (2) TempodClient records each event in `events` before it applies it. If applying throws (for example, the CredentialDO RPC for credential.changed fails), the event is dropped as a duplicate when resent and is never applied, so a Codex refresh is lost. The container API calls match worker-runtime.d.ts and the egress rules match spec 01. I could not run typecheck because dependencies are not installed in this worktree, and I could not check Better Auth's validateUserInfo option against real types.

findings.text: No test files and no vitest config in the change. CLAUDE.md rule 14 (every server function, op step and tempod request has a test, DO tests use @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers) and rule 15 (bun run test passes) are not met. The 06 definition of done also requires a failure-case test for each new server function, op step and tempod request.

evidence.why: None of the 64 changed files is a test, and there is no vitest.config.ts. Vitest's default passWithNoTests=false makes `vitest run` print 'No test files found' and exit with code 1. So `turbo run test`, and therefore `bun run test`, fails at this head. The repo rules say this must pass before a change is finished.

findings.text: The event row is inserted before the event is applied. If onEvent throws, the (incarnation, seq) is already stored, so a resend is dropped as a duplicate. Later events then advance tempodAckedSeq past it, so tempod never resends it. The event is permanently lost. Concrete case: credential.changed calls core.credentials().offerCodexAuth(...), a cross-DO RPC that can throw (DO reset, overload). The refreshed Codex auth.json is never stored or pushed to other lease holders, so their older refresh token may stop working (spec 01 Codex refresh sync, AT-11). The insert and the apply should be atomic: apply, then record; or delete the row if applying fails.

evidence.why: When onEvent rejects, the chain's catch only logs the error. The events row stays, so the same seq returns early with inserted.length === 0 on any later delivery. markApplied runs for the next seq, which moves tempodAckedSeq past the failed one, so tempod (01: resend seq > lastAckedSeq) never resends it. The work is lost instead of retried.

findings.text: I could not check the sign-in owner check against the real Better Auth 1.7.7 types, because better-auth is not installed in this worktree. If `user.validateUserInfo` is not a real option, a non-owner GitHub account can sign in and get user, session and account rows. Server functions still fail closed through requireOwner/isOwner, but AT-1 expects that account to be refused at sign-in. Confirm by running typecheck: `satisfies BetterAuthOptions` would reject an unknown property.

evidence.why: The only proof is in the type system, which I could not run here.

findings.text: D1 migrations are not generated. migrations_dir points to src/db/migrations, which does not exist in the change, so the D1 tables (user, projects, workspaces, ...) would never be created. 06 repo layout lists db/migrations/.

evidence.why: The directory is not present at the head commit.

findings.text: If the call to WorkspaceDO.init fails or its acknowledgement is lost after the D1 insert, the D1 row stays in state 'creating' with no DO data. For branch or PR sources, its active-branch unique index then makes every new create on that branch fail with BRANCH_IN_USE. Not blocking: 03 may define cleanup elsewhere.

evidence.why: Nothing compensates for a failed init after the insert.
